prompt:
Product change: members can set themselves out of office and name a stand-in.

User stories

- As a member, I can mark myself away between two instants — the start counts, the end does not — and optionally name a delegate: another active member of the same workspace, never myself. I can add a short note. Setting it again replaces it; I can also clear it. Whoever may change members' roles can set or clear anyone's absence; everyone else only their own. Anyone in the workspace can look up a member's absence.
- While I am away (from the start up to, but not including, the end):
  1. New assignments meant for me go to my delegate instead — whether an existing issue is assigned to me or an issue is created with me as its assignee. The issue is then the delegate's in every respect: the stored assignee, the announcements the assignment makes (events, audit), the alerts (my delegate is alerted as for any assignment; I am not), and who counts as the issue's assignee where that matters for permissions. Two exceptions: when I take an issue myself — I am the one assigning, and I assign it to me — nothing is redirected; and delegation is never chained — if my delegate is away too, the issue stays with my delegate. Without a delegate, assignments reach me as usual, and I am alerted as usual.
  2. Overdue alerts for issues assigned to me go to my delegate instead of me. Without a delegate they reach me as before. The overdue sweep itself is unchanged.
  3. A mention of me in a comment alerts both me and my delegate. The existing rules still apply: the comment's author is never alerted, each person gets at most one mention alert per comment (even when my delegate is mentioned directly in the same comment), and each recipient's own notification preferences apply.
  Issues that were already mine stay mine. Nothing moves back when the absence ends; the absence simply stops applying at its end.
- Membership: when a member is removed, their absence goes with them. When a member who is someone's delegate is removed, that delegation is dropped: the absence stays, now without a delegate, so nothing is ever redirected to someone who left.
- Workspaces are independent: an absence set in one workspace has no effect in another, even for a user who belongs to both.

Rules

- Validation: the end must be after the start (otherwise the request is rejected). The member must be an active member of the workspace — a removed member or a user from another workspace → `NotFoundError` (the one in `src/server/services/_support.ts`). The delegate, when given, must be an active member of the workspace (`NotFoundError` otherwise) and not the member themselves (rejected).
- Permissions: setting or clearing someone else's absence without the right → `PermissionDeniedError`. An `orgId` outside the actor's workspace → `TenantScopeError`, on every operation.
- Reading: `getAbsence` resolves to the stored absence as long as it has not ended — a scheduled absence that has not started yet is returned — and to `null` once it has ended or when none is set. Asking about someone who is not an active member → `NotFoundError`.
- "Away" is decided at the moment of the action: the assignment, the sweep, the comment.

Absences are persisted; a freshly migrated database (the way the test suite builds one) must have whatever you add.

API — add these exports:

In `src/types/member.ts`:

```ts
export interface MemberAbsence extends TenantScoped {
  readonly userId: UserId;
  readonly delegateUserId: UserId | null;
  readonly startsAt: IsoTimestamp;
  readonly endsAt: IsoTimestamp;
  readonly note: string | null;
}
```

In `src/schemas/member.ts`:

```ts
export const setAbsenceSchema = z.object({
  orgId: orgIdSchema,
  userId: userIdSchema,
  delegateUserId: userIdSchema.nullable().default(null),
  startsAt: isoTimestampSchema,
  endsAt: isoTimestampSchema,
  note: z.string().max(200).nullable().default(null),
});
export type SetAbsenceInput = z.infer<typeof setAbsenceSchema>;
```

In `src/server/services/member-service.ts`:

- `export async function setAbsence(actor: Actor, input: SetAbsenceInput): Promise<MemberAbsence>` — resolves to exactly what was stored.
- `export async function clearAbsence(actor: Actor, orgId: OrgId, userId: UserId): Promise<void>` — clearing when nothing is set is fine.
- `export async function getAbsence(actor: Actor, orgId: OrgId, userId: UserId): Promise<MemberAbsence | null>`

Update any visible test that encodes behaviour this change alters.

This is an `implement` task: edit the code and stop, as for a `fix` task. Do not write a summary and do not emit an ANSWER line.
notes: Implement (product spec, no bug.patch): out-of-office windows with a delegate. A persisted per-member window (start inclusive, end exclusive) with an optional stand-in that three existing mechanisms must now respect: assignment (both assignIssue and createIssue redirect to the delegate, except self-assignment, never chained), the overdue fan-out (alert goes to the delegate), and mentions (both the away member and the delegate, one alert per person per comment), plus member removal (deletes the leaver's absence and drops them as anyone's delegate) and tenant independence. Reference solution: 10 files, ~300 changed lines across types (MemberAbsence), zod (setAbsenceSchema), permission vocabulary + matrix + ownership escalation (member:set_absence, admin, own row escalated), drizzle schema + embedded migration (member_absences), a new repository, member-service (set/clear/get, activeDelegateFor, removal scrub), issue-service (redirect in create and assign) and notification-service (overdue + mention subscribers). Why it is hard: the redirect has two entry points (create with assignee is easy to miss), an exception (self-assignment) and a non-chaining rule; the overdue path is a bus subscriber fed by a sweep with its own clock; the mention rule interacts with notify()'s per-call recipient de-duplication and actor exclusion, so the natural "second notify() for the delegates" produces duplicate alerts; the window has an inclusive start and exclusive end evaluated at action time, and a scheduled (future) absence must be readable but inert; removal must scrub two things; permissions need a new action with an ownership escalation (memberResource.targetUserId) rather than a role branch. Trap: mention alerts for the delegate sent in a separate notify() call (naive B), and a window check that ignores the start (naive C). Hidden test: 16 cases (own set/replace/clear, admin-vs-others permissions, validation incl. removed target and removed delegate, tenancy on set/get/clear, scheduled/ended/non-member reads, assign redirect + event payload + alerts + direct assignment to the delegate, create-time redirect + issue.created payload, no delegate, window boundaries (before/last second/at end), no chaining, self-assignment both ways, overdue to delegate vs no-delegate, mentions incl. delegate mentioned directly, delegate as author and after the window, delegate leaves / member leaves, ownership rights of the redirected issue, same user in two workspaces). Validation: pristine tsc 0 / 617 pass; pristine+hidden 16/16 fail; solution: patch -p1 clean, tsc 0, full suite 633 pass, hidden 3x 16/16; naive A (redirect in assignIssue only; no overdue/mention handling; no removal scrub) 4/16 fail; naive B (complete, but delegates alerted through a second notify() call) 1/16 fail; naive C (complete, but "away" = "not ended yet", ignoring the start) 1/16 fail.
